chapters.title: Orchard Core Content Types
chapters.subtitle: Model the content of your site

steps.text: Every page, post and menu on an Orchard Core site is a content item, and its content type decides what it contains. In this video, you learn what content types, content parts and content fields are, and where you manage them.
A content item is one piece of content: a page, a blog post, a menu. It stores the values that editors enter, and it belongs to exactly one content type.
A content type describes a kind of content. It lists the parts that make up its items, in the order that editors see them.
A content part adds one capability, such as a title, a permalink or a body. A part can bring its own editor to the form, and several types can use the same part.
A content field holds a value of one kind: a line of text, a number, a date or an image. Fields live inside parts.
A type created in the admin gets a part of its own, named after the type. That part holds the fields you add to the type.

chapters.title: The Content Types page
chapters.subtitle: Every type of the site in one list

steps.text: Content types live under Design, Content Definition, Content Types. The page lists the types of the site, with a search box and a Create new type button.
Each row shows the display name of a type, and a badge with its technical name. The Blog Post type, for example, has the technical name BlogPost, written as one word.

Some rows have a second badge, the stereotype. A stereotype is a label that features use to find the types they work with: widgets have the Widget stereotype, and menu items have the MenuItem stereotype.

On the right, Create New Article opens the editor of an article, and List Items shows the articles that exist. Blog Post has no Create New Blog Post button, because its Creatable setting is off. Edit opens the type itself.
Let's open the Article type. At the top are its technical name, which is read only, and its display name, which is the name shown on screens.

Below the names are the settings of the type. Creatable and Listable decide whether editors can create and list items in the admin, and Draftable allows drafts. Stereotype, Category and Thumbnail are optional.
Under Fields, the type lists its own fields. Subtitle is a Text Field, and Banner Image is a Media Field. Each one holds a single value, a line of text or an image.
Under Parts, the type lists its parts, in the order that editors see them: Title, Autoroute, HtmlBody, and Article.
The last part is named after the type. It is the part that holds the fields above, and it is the only one without Edit and Remove buttons.
Title, Autoroute and HtmlBody are parts that features provide. Edit opens the settings of a part in this type, and Remove takes the part off the type.
Add Parts lists the parts you can add to the type, each with a short description.
Back on the type, Add Field asks for a display name, a technical name and a field type. The field types include Boolean Field, Date Field, Media Field, Numeric Field and Text Field.

chapters.title: From type to editor
chapters.subtitle: What editors fill in and visitors see

steps.text: Let's click Create New Article. The form follows the type: the parts add their editors in the order of the type, and the fields appear with the part that holds them.
Title comes from the Title part, and Permalink from Autoroute. The body comes from HtmlBody. The Article part adds its two fields, Subtitle and Banner Image.

Let's leave the form without saving and open the About page, an article of this site. Its title is the heading, its subtitle sits below the heading, its banner image fills the header, and the body follows.
The type sits behind both screens. Add a field to the type, and every article gets a place to fill it in. A theme can then display the value.
Parts have a page of their own, under Design, Content Definition, Content Parts. It lists the parts you can configure, with a Create new part button for adding your own.
Features add parts such as Title and Autoroute. A part you create joins the same list: Contact Details, for example, groups a phone number and a website.
Let's open Contact Details. It shows its names and a description. Attachable lets other types add the part, and Reusable lets one type add it more than once.
Under Fields, Contact Details lists Phone and Website. Any type that adds the part gets both fields in its editor.
That is the content model of Orchard Core: types made of parts, parts that hold fields, and the pages where you manage them. Thanks for watching.
